## What it is

<!-- KEEP:what-it-is:START -->
The business-module mechanism (ADR-MODULE-001 … 004). The core reads every business module's manifest
(`META-INF/erp/modules/<code>.yaml`) at startup into `ModuleCatalogApi`, and decides per tenant, from
`CORE_TENANT_MODULE`, which modules are entitled (`ModuleEntitlementApi`): enabled, not past `VALID_UNTIL`, and every
module it `depends` on entitled. An unentitled module is hidden from `GET /api/v1/sec/menu`, its authorities leave
the caller's effective set (each `@PreAuthorize` of it answers 403), its permissions cannot be granted, and its
`api-paths` answer 403 `MODULE_NOT_ENTITLED`. Rows are written by the platform operator
(`PUT /api/v1/platform/tenants/{tenantId}/modules/{code}`) or by the signed licence loaded at startup
(`erp.core.modules.license.file` / `.public-key`, Ed25519). With no manifest nothing changes.

Since 1.6.0 (CCR-MNT-001, ADR-MODULE-005) a manifest also declares `home-cards`: key figures of the shared home screen,
each valued by the module's one `HomeCardProvider` bean. `HomeCardApi.cardsForCurrentUser()` and
`GET /api/v1/modules/home-cards` return only the cards whose module is entitled for the tenant and whose permission the
caller holds, valued inside the request tenant within `erp.core.modules.home-cards.timeout-ms` (`UNAVAILABLE` when the
provider throws or is too slow), ordered by `order`, module code, key, with titles from the module's bundle. A card
whose permission or target the module does not contribute, or a module with cards and no provider, stops startup.
<!-- KEEP:what-it-is:END -->

## When to use it

<!-- KEEP:when-to-use:START -->
Whenever a product is sold per module: give each module a manifest and let the core gate it. Read
`ModuleEntitlementApi.isEntitled(code)` only to adapt a screen of a module that is always present; never to protect an
operation — the core already refuses it. A key figure of your module on the home screen is a `home-cards` entry plus a
`HomeCardProvider` (1.6.0): the core, not the module, decides who sees it.
<!-- KEEP:when-to-use:END -->

## How to call it

<!-- KEEP:how-to-call:START -->
```yaml
# leasing/src/main/resources/META-INF/erp/modules/leasing.yaml
module:
  code: leasing
  version: 1.0.0
  name: {ar: التأجير, en: Leasing}
  package: com.acme.rental.leasing
  permission-modules: [LEASING]          # contributed by LeasingPermissions in that package
  api-paths: [/api/v1/leasing/**]
  events:
    publishes: [leasing.ContractActivated]
  home-cards:                            # 1.6.0 — one entry per card, valued by LeasingHomeCards below
    - key: due-today
      title-key: leasing.home.due-today            # in the module's i18n bundle (spring.messages.basename)
      description-key: leasing.home.due-today.description
      permission: PERM_LEASING_PAYMENTS_VIEW       # contributed by LeasingPermissions
      order: 10
      target: LEASING_PAYMENTS                     # a screen of permission module LEASING
```

```java
// the one provider of the module's cards: read-only, called inside the request tenant
@Component
public class LeasingHomeCards implements HomeCardProvider {
    @Override public String moduleCode() { return "leasing"; }
    @Override public HomeCardValue value(String cardKey, HomeCardContext context) {
        return new HomeCardValue(paymentRepository.countDueOn(LocalDate.ofInstant(context.asOf(), ZoneId.systemDefault())));
    }
}

// adapt an always-present screen to an optional module
if (moduleEntitlementApi.isEntitled("maintenance")) {
    sections.add(maintenanceSection());
}
```

A single deployment's licence is issued with `java governance/tools/license/LicenseTool.java sign …` and configured
with `erp.core.modules.license.file` and `erp.core.modules.license.public-key`.
<!-- KEEP:how-to-call:END -->

## Do not rebuild

<!-- KEEP:do-not-rebuild:START -->
A licence or subscription check inside a module, a module on/off flag in settings, a menu filter per module, a
second table of enabled features, a branch on the deployment mode, a dashboard endpoint of the module's own or a
home card that checks its licence or permission itself.
